original.description: Objective:To develop European suppliers for the manufacture of high strength (HS) and high modulus (HM) carbonfibres for use in space systems.Description:Carbon fibres are one of the main components used in the development of lightweight structures for spaceapplications, especially high-strength and high modulus carbon fibres. These types of carbon fibres providehigh strength/weight andhigh stiffness/weight ratio in composite structures, ensuring both mechanicalperformance and dimensional stability for composites.High performance composite materials are widelyused in ESA launch vehicles, as well as primary structures of spacecrafts (such as Sentinels or Galileo) or robotic exploration platforms. According to a market study, the demand for carbon fibres for polymercomposite materials for space applications in Europe between 2023 and 2032 is estimated at approximately450 t.High-performance carbon fibres qualified for space flight are currently sourced from outside Europe and/orlinked to non-EU IP and export regimes, representing a strategic dependency. There have been someprojects on the development of pilot lines for carbon fibre manufacturing, such as the EUCARBON (FP7)and Space Carbon (H2020) activities, but the developed manufacturing capabilities are still in their earlystages and without clear plans on industrialization and utilization of the products. There are some limitedmanufacturing plants in Europe, however most of them use precursors (raw materials) that are imported,which again leads to foreign dependence. There are currently no existing, readily available and qualifiedcarbon fibres with a fully sovereign supply chain in Europe.The activity will focus onthe mechanical characterization, processability and industrialization, and conformity with ESA qualification standards. Its objective is to strengthen the development of a robust and autonomous European supply chain. The scope of the work targets RD activities carried out with European companies striving to replicateor exceedthe performance of competing solutions originating from outside Europe.Therefore, the following, not exhaustive, tasks shall be executed:- Identification of a fully European supply chain (including precursors and prepregging) to be assessed for their material systems and processes compatibility with space applications. Preferably define a supply chain able to realize prepregs from HM fibers and a supply chain to realize HS fiber tow for filament winding.- A characterization of the identified material systems for space applications, both at fiber level and at laminatelevel. Laminate level characterization shall be performed on samples manufactured using processes thatare common in space industry. Preferably autoclave process of prepregs with high modulus fibers andfilament winding with high strength fiber system. Benchmark results against ESA-qualified, non-Europeanmaterial systems to identify performance gaps and qualification needs.- Manufacture breadboards of representative space structural components using the identified HM and HSmaterial systems and relative processes. In this phase of the project the involvement of already establishedEuropean space composite structures designers, manufacturers and test houses is highlyrecommended.- Develop a database based on the acquired results and provide recommendations for standardization, furtherdevelopment and potential qualification and industrialization paths including a preliminary budget and time estimate.- An overview of the steps needed towards industrialization of a product of high-quality, assessment of facilities wrt re-use/adapt vs build dedicated one, long-term commercial viability plan (including discussions with the end users, lessons learned from other industries or other countries should be incorporated in this plan, for example ways to reduce the energy needed in a production planned).

However, European sources of quartz-based oscillatorsare becoming more limited, and these solutions are expensive, with a form factor and power consumption that becomes challenging when incorporating into highly integrated payloads. Current state-of-art oscillators based on microelectromechanical(MEMS) resonators display competitive phase noise and frequency stability performance compared to quartz-based solutions, but thereare no European or Canadian sources of such products. Important advantages of such MEMS resonators compared to quartz-based oscillatorcan be seen, where MEMS achieves performance in between the Temperature Controlled Crystal Oscillator (TCXO) and Oven ControlledCrystal Oscillators (OCXOs) but with the advantage of their extremely small form factor, low power consumption and integration capability with Silicon process. One more important aspect is that the MEMS fundamentalmode frequency can be much higher than that of aQuartz crystal, whereas cost reduction is expected at lower frequencies and better performance at higher frequencies.This activity will design, manufacture of an engineering model oscillator chip based on European microelectromechanical technology in the 10 and500 MHz frequency range. The performance shall be suitable for a range of application scenarios in telecom payloads. The engineering model chip shall be built and tested in a critical environment, including thermal test

original.description: Objective: To model the hypersonic flow around critical points of the re-entry of a upper stage vehicle, accounting for the catalytic properties of a Si-O-C ceramics, and for the chemical modifications of the surface exposed to the air.Description: There is a renewed interest in the implementation of reusable vehicles for in-orbit operation. A critical aspect in the lifetime of a space vehicle is to improve the durability of the thermal protection structures, to limit the replacement of the thermal shield. Ultra-high temperature ceramics (UHTC) materials, based on the Si-O-C compounds with dedicated coatings (boride, molybdenum etc.) demonstrated to be a good choice, due to their capability to resist and survive above 1500 K. To fully evaluate the response of any material in suchextreme operating conditions, it is also imperative to determine the catalysis in high temperature gas, strongly affecting the surface heat flux. Moreover, the interaction of the material coatings with dissociated gases such as oxygen and nitrogen, induces variations on the material properties. The technology to be developed is to model accurately the complex physical processes at the gas surface interface during ascent and descent, in which different coatings are experimental tested validating the predictive capabilitiesof the numerical models. The model will include advanced kinetics, using a hybrid state-to-state -Multi-Temperature (StS-MT) derived from the StS, where the vibrational degrees of freedom are described by the vibrational temperature, while electronic excited states are treated as independent species, in order to estimate the radiative properties. This activity encompasses the following tasks:- Development of a chemical model of air interacting with the Si-O-C ceramic material, in dissociation regime; - Development of a hybrid StS-MT kinetic model - Develop a database for thermodynamic properties and of transport cross sections for air including Si-O-C species - Implementation of kinetics and transport in a numerical tool for hypersonic flows for the reliable simulation, flat plate/coupons - Model chemical gas surface interaction, chemical stability, roughness, thickness, stability of coatings, catalyst by experimental plasma testing of different samples, thermal optical properties, emission spectroscopy - Numerical modelling and testing thermal bounding of the silica based substrate bounding with the coating, testing of the attachment devices - Evaluation of differentceramics suitable for the orbital entry conditions.

original.description: Objective: To develop a comprehensive set of rigorously tested tools that ensures monitoring, risk assessment, and collision avoidance for close proximity operations.Description: Past activities related to Close Proximity Operations (CPO) highlighted the need ofdeveloping low impact velocity tools that can verify and validate that the servicer spacecraft (SC) maintains a collision risk probability of less than given threshold (e.g 10^-4) with the client SC during CPO. For missions involving multiple SC in close formation, the design of manoeuvres to avoid collisions with catalogue objects not belonging to the formation requires to take into account all SC of the formation, e.g. an avoidance manoeuvre performed by one SC of the formation shall not trigger an inner-formation collision risk but rather minimise disturbance to the formation while ensuring the required risk reduction. This activity aims at developing a comprehensive set of tools (e.g. DRAMA like tool, prototype software for formation flying) that ensure monitoring, risk assessment, and collision avoidance during close proximity operations (including formation flying). This activity encompasses the followingtasks: - Develop and refine software tools that model the trajectory of both the target and servicer. - Develop algorithms that identify safe trajectories for close approaches and include collision avoidance features. - Develop tools that perform uncertainty propagation to estimate the likelihood of a collision between the servicer and client. - Identify sensor systems capable of providing design and operational level data about the relative positions, velocities, and orientations of both the servicer and the target. - Conduct virtual testing within the developed tools to simulate close approach and rendezvous operations in various scenarios. - Develop mathematical models of constraints and requirements and prototype a software solution suitable for realistic scenarios.

original.description: Summary Description The proposed activity is will support the preparation for the ERASE Phase A. ERASE aims to prepare the removalof large, non-cooperative and unprepared objects in low Earth orbit, initially considering Metop and Sentinel-1 targets (starting with METOP-A and S1B, both being decommissioned), thereby supporting ESA's Space Safety Programme and the transition towards a circular economy in space. This activity will establish and demonstrate ground-based laser-ranging measurement, modelling and analysis capabilities to characterise the attitude state and tumbling behaviour of non-cooperative, unprepared targets, with initial focus on Metop and Sentinel-1 targets. The output is essential and urgent for the ERASE Phase A study. Without this information available at the start of Phase A, there is a risk that the technical feasibility of the mission is incorrectly assessed. The target spin rate is adesign driver for the servicer delta-V and operations timeline, the relative navigation subsystem, and the robotic capture sizing and loads. The spin-axis orientation drives the safe approach direction and the capture strategy. In addition, the probability of very low spin-rate cases must be understood, as such cases may lead to long durations in unfavourable attitude conditions for target power generation, thermal control and ground contact. The challenge is that the targets are not prepared with cooperative markers or laser retro-reflectors that would facilitate attitude reconstruction. The attitude state must therefore be reconstructed from non-cooperative laser-ranging observables, making use of time-of-flight/range measurements, return-signal characteristics, pass geometry, target geometry, known or estimated surface properties, and attitude-dynamics modelling. Where beneficial, the laser-ranging data maybe complemented by passive optical or radar observations.The activity will assess the feasibility, achievable accuracy and uncertainty of attitude determination and dynamics-based propagation from ground. It will characterise and propagate target dynamics, in particular spin rate and spin-axis orientation, and will provide statistically meaningful uncertainty envelopes for ERASE Phase A design trade-offs. The activity will also prepare the capability to perform repeated attitude characterisation campaigns in support of ERASE. The attitude state of non-cooperative targets may evolve over time due to environmental torques and target-specific dynamics; therefore, measurements may be required not only during the present feasibility phase, but also before launch, to confirm that the target conditions remain within the design assumptions, and potentially at intermediate points during mission preparation. A dedicated task will assess the applicability of the developed measurement and modelling methods to a broader range of large, unprepared, non-cooperative low Earth orbit targets beyond Metop and Sentinel-1, identifying the key target properties, observation conditions and limitations that determine feasibility.

The attitude state must therefore be reconstructed from non-cooperative laser-ranging observables, making use of time-of-flight/range measurements, return-signal characteristics, pass geometry, target geometry, known or estimated surface properties, and attitude-dynamics modelling. Where beneficial, the laser-ranging data maybe complemented by passive optical or radar observations.The activity will assess the feasibility, achievable accuracy and uncertainty of attitude determination and dynamics-based propagation from ground. It will characterise and propagate target dynamics, in particular spin rate and spin-axis orientation, and will provide statistically meaningful uncertainty envelopes for ERASE Phase A design trade-offs. The activity will also prepare the capability to perform repeated attitude characterisation campaigns in support of ERASE. The attitude state of non-cooperative targets may evolve over time due to environmental torques and target-specific dynamics; therefore, measurements may be required not only during the present feasibility phase, but also before launch, to confirm that the target conditions remain within the design assumptions, and potentially at intermediate points during mission preparation. A dedicated task will assess the applicability of the developed measurement and modelling methods to a broader range of large, unprepared, non-cooperative low Earth orbit targets beyond Metop and Sentinel-1, identifying the key target properties, observation conditions and limitations that determine feasibility.
